---
title: "Conventional IRT and the Local Independence Assumption"
---

## The conventional model family

*Rasch/1PL, 2PL, 3PL, graded response, (generalized) partial credit, MIRT and
bi-factor — the Level-0 baselines of the model ladder, implemented via `mirt`
and `TAM`.*

## Local independence, formally

For a response vector $Y_i = (Y_{i1}, \ldots, Y_{iJ})$:

$$P(Y_i = y_i \mid \theta_i) = \prod_j P(Y_{ij} = y_{ij} \mid \theta_i, \xi_j)$$

*State the assumption precisely; distinguish it from unidimensionality.*

## Where the assumption strains

*Local dependence, testlets, item bundles, speededness, multidimensionality —
the persistent practical realities conventional models treat as nuisances.
Q3-style residual diagnostics and limited-information fit statistics as the
detection toolkit.*

## Existing accommodations

*Testlet response theory, bi-factor/two-tier models, latent class IRT — what
each concedes to dependence, and at what interpretive cost.*
